reason: Survives the feasibility lens only as the two-stage part (1); part (2), raising the gate from 8.0 to 9.5 h, should be dropped. (a) Code: the new code sits inside safetail_divins_call's try/except, so it is fail-soft (FF dummy 2/2 PASS, CSV == exp56 on forced failure). It is byte-identical when off behind a new knob. The exactness bound holds: score = pu*pv*pc^alpha <= pu, since p <= 1 after the softmax mean with monotone rounding, and alpha >= 0. NaN is rejected on both routes. (b) Two caveats. Stage batches change the cuDNN batch shapes, so identity is proven only on the 4 dummies; a flip on the hidden set needs a score within ~1e-6 of 0.4 or a near-tie inside the cap, so the impact is ~0. Also, pruned triples move from the below_threshold counter to the missing_p counter, so the full 'divinsert:' log line will differ; gate on the CSV sha256 plus the eligible/added/(orphan, steal) fields. (c) Saving measured on CPU: on the exp56 output, unique parents are 0.38-0.48 of the scored nodes (orphan triples; the counts match the exp58 log). Scoring costs ~4 s + 8.7 ms/node. So the saving is ~45-55%, not ~2/3: ~30-35 s/clip, ~0.8-1.0 h on ~100 hidden clips. The proposed '>= 50% fewer nodes scored' gate is borderline. (d) Schedule: it needs no LB slot of its own. It rides on K3 (S4 26.09) or K3b/K4 with one ~25 min dummy and 2-3 agent hours at the lowest R10 priority, which is well before the R8 cut-off of 27.09 12:00. It reduces hidden runtime, so no headroom problem. (e) Part (2) is mis-costed. Repair runs clip by clip after the GPU phase. Insertion time spent between 8.0 and 9.5 h uses up the repair budget of later clips. With R clips left at 8.0 h, raising the gate pushes clips past the 9.5 h repair deadline into degraded mode (no readmit/gapfill, worth far more than the insertion) whenever R*57 s < 5400 s < R*(57 + insertion) s. So it is not 'at most one clip'. The EV is tiny either way, which is why this is not refuted but conditional.
fix: Ship only part (1), and keep DIVINS_DEADLINE_S = 28800; the speed-up itself is the insurance. If the gate must move, move it to at most 9.0 h, and only after the two-stage speed-up is in. Implementation: stage 1 = score_nodes on the sorted unique u. Stage 2 = score the sorted unique c1/v of the triples with p_par(u) >= DIVINS_THRESH that are not already scored. Merge into _dv_node_p. Clear DIVINS_BUNDLE['prepared_frames'] only after stage 2. Put it behind a new knob DIVINS_TWOSTAGE (default 0 = current code path verbatim). Add a unit test with a mock scorer: the insert_divisions edges equal the one-stage result on random p, including p = 1.0 and NaN. Dummy gate: K2+D4 twin with FORKMID off, sha256(submission.csv) == the K2 dummy; per clip, eligible/added/orphan/steal are equal; nodes_scored down >= 35%; divins_sec_score down >= 30%; no 'DIVINS FAILED'. On any mismatch, drop without debugging. Trigger: build it only if the K2 latency, observed ~08:00-09:00 UTC 26.09, is > ~7.3 h, or if a later rider needs the runtime. Otherwise skip it and save the agent hours. Bundle it into K3/K3b/K4 and never give it its own slot.
realistic_gain: Score: ~+0.00002..+0.0001 private EV (insurance that insertion is not skipped on the last clips in a slow hidden run; ~0 in the likely world where K2 is <= 7.5 h). Runtime: -0.8..-1.0 h of hidden runtime (measured unique-parent fraction 0.38-0.48, ~45-55% of the ~66 s/clip scoring), which is useful headroom for other riders. Cost: 2-3 agent hours and one ~25 min GPU dummy; no LB slot.
